title: Scalar and table-valued functions
summary: Write UDFs, understand inline vs multi-statement TVFs, and avoid scalar-UDF performance traps.

items: Create scalar, inline TVF, and multi-statement TVF.
Explain why inline TVFs and scalar UDF inlining matter for performance.

blocks.body: User-defined functions encapsulate reusable logic, but scalar UDFs historically hurt performance.

terms.definition: A table-valued function whose body is a single SELECT; expands like a view for the optimizer.
SQL Server 2019+ feature that inlines eligible scalar UDFs for big speedups.

blocks.body: Prefer **inline table-valued functions** over multi-statement TVFs — the optimizer can expand and optimize them. **Scalar UDF inlining** (Intelligent Query Processing) automatically inlines eligible scalar functions.

items.mistake: Row-by-row scalar UDFs in SELECT lists on large sets.
items.fix: Rewrite as an inline TVF via APPLY, or rely on scalar UDF inlining.

tips: Inline TVF good, multi-statement TVF often bad for cardinality estimation.

blocks.body: Favor inline TVFs; know that scalar UDF inlining can rescue legacy scalar functions.
